Run a plan

Source: R/run_plan.R
run_plan.Rd

run_plan() runs every analysis of the plnr plan p, in this R session or on workers new R sessions. It stops when an analysis fails, and then it prints each failed analysis with its error.

Usage

run_plan(p, workers = 1)

Arguments

p

A plan from plnr::Plan$new(), with data from add_data() and analyses from add_analyses().

workers

The number of R sessions that run the analyses, one whole number of 1 or more.

Value

Invisibly, a named list with one element for each analysis of the plan, in the order of the plan. Element i is the value of the action function of analysis i. Give it to save_results().

Details

With workers = 1, run_plan() calls p$run_all() in this R session.

With workers 2 or more, run_plan() needs the packages doParallel and foreach. It starts a PSOCK cluster of workers new R sessions with parallel::makePSOCKcluster(), registers it with doParallel::registerDoParallel(), and calls p$run_all() with the foreach path of plnr. A PSOCK cluster does not fork, so it also works on Windows. Before the run, run_plan() gives each worker these:

  • the library paths of this R session, from .libPaths().

  • the packages attached in this R session, in the order of search(), for example data.table after library(data.table) in the run script.

  • the kind of random number generator of this R session, from RNGkind().

  • every object of the environment that initialize_project() sourced the functions folder into, .GlobalEnv by default. So a data function and an action function find CFG and the other functions of the folder. A plnr plan and .Random.seed are left out. Each object is copied to each worker, so keep large objects out of that environment.

  • the paths in org::project, such as org::project$data_raw.

run_plan() does not copy the R options, for example options(digits = 3), and no other state of this R session.

After the run, run_plan() stops the cluster and registers the sequential foreach backend, also after an error.

plnr calls each data function once for each scenario and simulation, see add_data(). Each data function and each analysis sets its own seed before it runs, see add_analyses(). Take a function that depends only on its arguments, the objects of the functions folder such as CFG, the attached packages and the seed. Its results with workers = 1 and with workers = 2 are identical(). A function that reads an R option or another state of the main R session can give other results on a worker. A data.table loses its self-reference on the way back from a worker, and run_plan() gives it a new one with data.table::setalloccol(). It does this for each data.table in a value or in a plain list in a value, at any depth.

run_plan() runs every analysis, also after an analysis fails. An error in an action function fails that analysis, and an error in a data function fails each analysis that gets the data. This is the same with 1 worker and with more. After the run, run_plan() prints each failed analysis with its name and its full error message with cat(), and then it stops. R cuts an error message at 1000 bytes by default, and cat() does not. pbn then saves nothing, because save_results() needs the value of run_plan(). The results files of an earlier run stay as they are.

The value carries the attribute pbn_run, a stamp of the plan. It holds no count of the runs, so two runs of one plan can be identical(). save_results() stops on a value without the stamp of its plan.

run_plan() sets use_foreach of the plan: FALSE for 1 worker and TRUE for more.

After initialize_project(), run_plan() first computes the md5 of each raw data file again when its size or its modification time changed. The value carries the md5 in its stamp, and save_results() writes it to manifest$data_md5.

For a data function with cache = TRUE, run_plan() needs initialize_project() first, and it prints one line for each scenario and simulation. The section Cache of add_data() gives the rules. A data function that returns a cohort::CohortPipeline runs on the worker, and only its data.table and its exclusion table come back. The section A cohort as the data of add_data() gives the rules.

See also

vignette("pbn"), which builds and runs a small fake project.

Other plan: add_analyses(), add_data(), cohort_data()

Examples

CFG <- list(scenarios = data.frame(scenario = c("real", "null"), sims = 2))
p <- plnr::Plan$new()
pbn::add_data(p, "d", fn = function(scenario, sim) {
  return(data.frame(x = stats::rnorm(5)))
})
pbn::add_analyses(
  p,
  pbn::scenarios(CFG),
  name = "mean_x",
  fn = function(data, argset) return(data.frame(mean = mean(data$d$x)))
)
r <- pbn::run_plan(p)
r[["null__sim_0002__mean_x__1"]]
#>          mean
#> 1 -0.06696949
